A short guide What is ADHD? A brain that runs on interest, not importance.
The basics A difference in how the brain develops. It starts in childhood and often carries on into adulthood. It’s not laziness, bad parenting or too much screen time.
Not a lack of attention Trouble steering it. Boring tasks slip away. Interesting ones can swallow hours. That’s called hyperfocus.
The brain’s manager Executive function gets overloaded. Starting tasks Planning Sense of time Working memory Big feelings Impulses
It looks different in different people Three common patterns Quiet, daydreamy ADHD is often missed, especially in girls and women. Mostly inattentive Mostly hyperactive-impulsive Combined
How common? About 6–10% of Australian children. And about 2–6% of adults. It runs in families: genes explain most of the risk.
What helps Plenty, and it works. Understanding it Reminders & routines Medication Coaching or therapy Sleep & movement School or work adjustments
The goal A life that fits your brain. Energy, creativity and hyperfocus are real strengths. The aim is fewer things working against you.
